# Previews: next steps

Generated by `patchy setup previews` (patchy v0.12.40) for the **existing edge: Ingress class nginx** recipe on **eks**.
Previews will be served at `https://<project>-<issue>.acme-previews.dev`, and viewers sign in at `https://preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`.
Nothing here has been applied: run the steps below in order. Running `patchy setup previews` again shows what would
change before it replaces a file, and never draws a new Dex client secret unless you pass
`--rotate dex-client-secret`.

## Files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT-STEPS.md` | This file. |
| `answers.yaml` | Every answer, the edge and the CLI version: a re-run starts from it. No secret. |
| `manifests/certificate.yaml` | The cert-manager Certificate for `*.<suffix>` and the sign-in host. |
| `patchy-previews.values.yaml` | patchy's chart values for previews, layered after your own. |
| `secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml` | The same secret, in Dex's namespace, for its static client (0600). |
| `secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml` | The relay's Dex client secret, in the release namespace (0600). |

The files under `secrets/` (mode 0600) hold the only copy of the Dex client secret. Apply them, or encrypt them (sops,
sealed-secrets) before they go anywhere else; never commit them as they are.

## 1. Before you start

- patchy is installed in namespace `patchy` as release `patchy`, with `intentController.enabled: true`
  in your values: previews are built for intents, and the preview-controller needs intent-controller.
- NetworkPolicy is enforced. On EKS, turn on the VPC CNI's network policy support (on Auto Mode, `enable-network-policy-controller: "true"` in the `amazon-vpc-cni` ConfigMap in kube-system), or run a CNI that enforces it.
- cert-manager runs in the cluster, and the Issuer `preview-dns01` in
  namespace `patchy` can answer an ACME DNS-01 challenge for both `*.acme-previews.dev` and `preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`
  (a wildcard needs DNS-01). The two names sit on different registrable domains, so usually in two DNS zones: the
  solver's credential must answer for both. See "The wildcard certificate" in
  `docs/configuration/preview-gateway.md` for an Issuer to start from.

## 2. Preview nodes

Every slot Pod selects `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews=true` and tolerates the taint `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only=true:NoExecute`. Add at least one node with both, set when it registers so no other Pod lands on it first. Use a managed node group with `labels: {patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews: "true"}` and `taints: [{key: patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only, value: "true", effect: NoExecute}]` (eksctl's `managedNodeGroups`, or terraform's `aws_eks_node_group`). On EKS Auto Mode, see `preview.nodeIsolation.eksAutoMode` in the chart's values: it can render the NodePool and NodeClass.

## 3. Preview image pulls

Preview images are `123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/acme/patchy/previews/<app>:sha-<commit>`. Slot Pods may not reference a Secret, so pulls are
the node's own: give the preview nodes' IAM role ECR pull on `acme/patchy/previews/*` only.

## 4. Dex

Add the relay's static client to Dex's configuration, with its one redirect URI:

```yaml
staticClients:
  - id: patchy-preview-auth
    name: patchy previews
    secretEnv: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
    redirectURIs:
      - https://preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev/dex/callback
```

Give Dex the secret in that environment variable from the Secret in its namespace (with Dex's Helm chart:
`envVars: [{name: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: patchy-preview-auth-client, key: clientSecret}}}]`),
then roll Dex:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml
```

## 5. TLS

```sh
kubectl apply -f manifests/certificate.yaml
kubectl -n patchy wait certificate/preview-wildcard --for=condition=Ready --timeout=10m
```

Both Ingresses name its Secret, `preview-wildcard-tls`. Put no `cert-manager.io/*issuer` annotation on either: a
second Certificate for the same Secret would fight this one.

## 6. Install

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml
helm upgrade patchy oci://ghcr.io/devthenet-labs/patchy/charts/patchy -n patchy --version 0.12.40 \
  -f <your values> -f patchy-previews.values.yaml
```

One upgrade: the gateway needs no permit stage. `previewController.config.apiServerCIDR: auto` is looked up at render time, so it needs `helm upgrade` against the cluster (not
`helm template` or a GitOps render, which must set the kubernetes Service's `/32` instead).

## 7. DNS

Point two records at the edge's address:

- `*.acme-previews.dev`
- `preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`

The address is the Ingress controller's load balancer (`kubectl -n patchy get ingress patchy-preview-gateway`
once it is admitted). `previewAuth.gateway.forwardedHops: 1` holds when the controller sees the client's address
(its Service has `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`, or it trusts the PROXY protocol); behind a cloud L7 load balancer
that also appends `X-Forwarded-For`, it is 2.

## 8. Check

```sh
patchy check previews -n patchy
```

Every line should PASS before the first intent's preview is opened.

## Rolling back

In reverse order, all by deletion:

1. Set `previewAuth.gateway.enabled: false` (or `preview.enabled: false`) and run the same `helm upgrade`.
2. `kubectl delete -f manifests/certificate.yaml`
3. Remove the two DNS records.
4. Remove the static client from Dex, and delete the Secrets (`kubectl delete -f secrets/`).
5. Delete what the chart keeps on uninstall, as `docs/intents/preview-sign-in.md` lists it.
